paragraphs.text: In several countries a street can exist on official maps and nowhere else. Such “paper roads” were drawn when land was divided for houses that were never built, and the plans were never cancelled.
paragraphs.label: A

paragraphs.text: For walkers this is sometimes good news: a paper road is public land, so it may give access to a beach or a hill across private fields. Hikers in New Zealand use old survey maps to find them.
paragraphs.label: B

paragraphs.text: Landowners see the matter differently. Fences are often built across these strips, and councils rarely have money for signs, so a walker may be certain of a right that nobody else can see on the ground.
paragraphs.label: C
